biotech-act.text: Parliament voted the amended Biotech Act directive on genetically modified micro-organisms and organs, by 351 votes to 176 with 132 abstentions.

Agence Europe reports that the committees adopted Marta Temido and Adam Jarubas's report on the directive on GMMs and organs on 10 November by 54 votes to 18 with 16 abstentions. Greens/EFA amendments allowing national bans were rejected.

cef-2028-2034.text: Parliament backed ITRE-TRAN's mandate to negotiate the Connecting Europe Facility 2028–2034 with the Council, by 451 votes to 173 with 38 abstentions.
Agence Europe reports that ITRE and TRAN adopted their position on the CEF on 10 November by 101 votes to 1 with 17 abstentions. They ask for €91.28bn, against €81.42bn in the Commission proposal.

digital-fairness-act.text: The Commission presented its proposal for a Digital Fairness Act, an update of EU consumer protection rules so that consumers get the same protection online as offline.

digital-networks-act.text: Telecom challengers including Iliad, Digi, Colt and 1&1 asked for stronger competition safeguards in Michał Kobosko's draft report and a mandatory nationwide switch from copper to fibre.

digital-omnibus-data.text: Member states agreed the Council's negotiating mandate. Talks with Parliament open once Parliament adopts its own position.

grids-package.text: Council and Parliament negotiators reached a provisional agreement on the grids package permitting directive on 18 November 2026. ITRE, plenary and the Council must still endorse it.
Agence Europe reports that Council and Parliament negotiators held the third and penultimate TEN-E trilogue on 10 November. The final round is planned for early December.

industrial-accelerator-act.text: Member states moved closer to agreement on the act's foreign investment chapter. They remain split on Commission waiver powers, the investment threshold and workforce rules, and Ireland aims for a Council position by end of November.

The joint INTA-ITRE-IMCO committee vote remains officially set for 1 December despite more than 5,000 amendments. The EPP is split, and a group around Christian Ehler and Jörgen Warborn wants the proposal rejected.
More than 5,000 amendments were tabled to the joint draft report. Dirk Gotink's amendments would open 'Made in Europe' to all trade and procurement-agreement partners.
The Committee of the Regions adopted its opinion on the act. Its rapporteur is Willy Borsus.

kids-act.text: Agence Europe reports that the European Data Protection Supervisor published an opinion on the KIDS Act on 12 November. It recommends that age verification duties apply only once privacy-preserving solutions are available across the EU.

mff-2028-2034.text: António Costa presented his MFF negotiating box on 21 November as the basis for the Special European Council of 26–27 November.
Agence Europe reports that the AGRI, BUDG and REGI committees will not vote on the National and Regional Partnership Plans regulation before January 2027. The vote had been planned for December.

Agence Europe reports that ITRE adopted its position on the European Competitiveness Fund on 10 November by 61 votes to 13 with 12 abstentions, and a negotiating mandate by 56 to 26. It raises the fund to €264bn for 2028–2034.

Agence Europe reports that Friedrich Merz asked António Costa in a letter of 6 November to link fair sharing of the 2027 Ukraine aid gap, about €70bn, to the MFF 2028–2034 talks. Finland and Estonia oppose the link.

More than 1,000 amendments were tabled to the draft Performance Regulation, about 300 on its results indicators. At a joint BUDG-CONT meeting on 4 November, the groups split over the do no significant harm principle.
Member states do not expect António Costa's negotiating box before the last week of November. Diplomats see the 17–18 December European Council as the most likely moment for a deal.

Parliament's Conference of Presidents backed turning committee positions on the Competitiveness Fund, Horizon Europe, fisheries and AgoraEU into negotiating mandates without a plenary vote, likely announced in mid-December.

Agriculture ministers agreed the Council's negotiating mandate on the post-2027 common agricultural policy on 26 October. Farm support would be paid through the National and Regional Partnership Plans.
Parliament's rapporteurs and shadows agreed compromise amendments on the European Competitiveness Fund on 22 October. ITRE is expected to adopt them on 10 November.

military-mobility.text: Agence Europe reports that negotiators agreed a five-day deadline for military transport permissions in normal times, but remain split on the crisis framework and EMERS. The next trilogue is set for 9 December.

tech-sovereignty-package.text: Agence Europe reports that the Irish Presidency tabled a new CADA compromise text in Council that relaxes the environmental provisions for acceleration areas.
MLex reports that the two MEPs leading Parliament work on the Cloud and AI Development Act set out a draft report that seeks to streamline approval procedures and address energy constraints.
